title: Untangling the Lantern Cord  (Desenredando el cordón de los farolillos)

segments.t: En el balcón del segundo piso sopla una brisa juguetona. Graham y Caleb trabajan hombro con hombro y recogen con cuidado, sobre la barandilla de madera, los dos cordones de farolillos enredados. Escúchalos primero de principio a fin.
Pull the left cord gently toward your hand, Graham — two lanterns hooked their wire handles.
Easy does it... lift the coral globe over the gold one, and they come apart clean.
Zero torn paper! Still, if the wind blows tomorrow evening, these two lines will touch again.
That is why I brought four light cedar dowels drilled at both ends from the cellar.
Wait — wooden spreader bars tied between parallel cords like rigging on a sailing ship?!
My uncle worked harbor boats in his youth; two parallel lines with spacers never twist.
Let me tie this cedar bar halfway — look how steady both cords ride now!
And clip each lantern handle closed with a tiny brass ring so none can jump free.
Architecturally AND nautically brilliant, Graham — watch them sway gently together in unison!
Not bad for a man who does not own a tablet computer, right, Caleb?
Every time I work beside you, Graham, I add another page to my notebook!
Come downstairs now — I have three dozen wooden clothespins waiting for Hannah at the front desk.
Subamos de nuevo al balcón y deshagamos el enredo réplica a réplica.
Pull the left cord gently toward your hand, Graham — two lanterns hooked their wire handles.
'Tira suavemente del cordón izquierdo hacia tu mano, Graham: dos farolillos se engancharon por sus asas de alambre.'
Easy does it... lift the coral globe over the gold one, and they come apart clean.
'Despacito y con cuidado... pasa el globo coral por encima del dorado y se separan limpiamente.'
Zero torn paper! Still, if the wind blows tomorrow evening, these two lines will touch again.
'¡Ni un papel roto! Aun así, si mañana por la tarde sopla el viento, estas dos cuerdas volverán a tocarse.'
That is why I brought four light cedar dowels drilled at both ends from the cellar.
'Por eso traje del sótano cuatro varillas ligeras de cedro perforadas en ambos extremos.'
Wait — wooden spreader bars tied between parallel cords like rigging on a sailing ship?!
'Espera, ¿¡barras separadoras de madera atadas entre cuerdas paralelas, como el aparejo de un velero!?'
My uncle worked harbor boats in his youth; two parallel lines with spacers never twist.
'Mi tío trabajó en barcos del puerto en su juventud; dos cuerdas paralelas con separadores nunca se retuercen.'
Let me tie this cedar bar halfway — look how steady both cords ride now!
'Déjame atar esta barra de cedro a mitad de camino: ¡mira qué estables van ahora las dos cuerdas!'
And clip each lantern handle closed with a tiny brass ring so none can jump free.
'Y cierra el asa de cada farolillo con una pequeña anilla de latón para que ninguno pueda soltarse.'
Architecturally AND nautically brilliant, Graham — watch them sway gently together in unison!
'¡Brillante desde el punto de vista arquitectónico Y náutico, Graham! ¡Mira cómo se mecen suavemente juntos, al unísono!'
Not bad for a man who does not own a tablet computer, right, Caleb?
'Nada mal para un hombre que no tiene ni una tableta, ¿verdad, Caleb?'
Every time I work beside you, Graham, I add another page to my notebook!
'¡Cada vez que trabajo a tu lado, Graham, añado otra página a mi cuaderno!'
Come downstairs now — I have three dozen wooden clothespins waiting for Hannah at the front desk.
'Baja ahora: tengo tres docenas de pinzas de madera esperando a Hannah en la recepción.'
Disfruta de la escena completa una vez más, al ritmo natural de la conversación.

Easy does it... lift the coral globe over the gold one, and they come apart clean.
Zero torn paper! Still, if the wind blows tomorrow evening, these two lines will touch again.

Wait — wooden spreader bars tied between parallel cords like rigging on a sailing ship?!
My uncle worked harbor boats in his youth; two parallel lines with spacers never twist.
Let me tie this cedar bar halfway — look how steady both cords ride now!
And clip each lantern handle closed with a tiny brass ring so none can jump free.
Architecturally AND nautically brilliant, Graham — watch them sway gently together in unison!
Not bad for a man who does not own a tablet computer, right, Caleb?

Come downstairs now — I have three dozen wooden clothespins waiting for Hannah at the front desk.
Gracias a unas barras separadoras dignas de un barco del puerto, los farolillos se mecen juntos sin enredarse ni una sola vez. ¡Hasta la próxima!
Take care!
